question: Who discovered a principle that states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Archimedes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The principle that states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object is known as** Archimedes' Principle.**
 
• Archimedes' Principle is attributed to Archimedes of Syracuse, **a Greek mathematician** and inventor who lived from approximately 287 to 212 BCE.
 
• The principle was described in his work **"On Floating Bodies."**
 
• This principle is** fundamental in fluid mechanics** and **explains why objects float or sink in fluids**.
 
• The** formula** for Archimedes' principle is** FB = ρVg,** where:
 
 
• FB: is the buoyant force 
 
• ρ: is the density of the fluid 
 
• V: is the volume of the object that is submerged or the volume
